final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the core evidentiary gaps: no remediation, no approved risk acceptance, and no closed legal determination on disclosure. That means the audit picture is unchanged from the initial report. The Actor's narrower framing is more accurate than a clean-certification claim, but it is still a reframing of the same record, not new proof that the policy condition was met. Proportionality does not support `compliant_with_caveats` here because the caveat is not merely descriptive; it is the unresolved compliance predicate itself. A caveated outcome could fit if the evidence showed the required disclosure was actually made, or legal/risk acceptance had formally closed the issue, while other residual risks remained. On this record, the material named-use-case limitation is still unresolved under the policy, so the proper outcome remains noncompliant.
remaining_concerns: The tax filing assistant gap remains a material limitation because it affects a named launch use case tied to two partner commitments.

Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so the policy predicate is unresolved on the current record.

No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance covering this unresolved limitation before launch.
Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and monitoring plans do not satisfy the separate pre-launch disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement.
